summary: This paper generalizes Pauli Check Sandwiching (PCS) from qubits to qudits of arbitrary dimension $d$ by constructing checks from Heisenberg-Weyl operators that deterministically map errors to unique ancilla readouts. The protocol achieves unit fidelity under joint post-selection on noiseless checks and is validated numerically across $d = 2$ to $9$, demonstrating error-mitigated fidelities above $97.5\%$ under realistic depolarizing noise.
motivation: While qudit platforms such as trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and neutral atoms enable high-dimensional quantum information processing (up to $d = 20$ demonstrated), effective error management techniques for qudits remain underdeveloped compared to qubit-based methods.
method: Generalized left and right Pauli checks are constructed using controlled $\mathcal{M}_d^n$ (shift) and $\mathcal{Z}_d^n$ (clock) operators from the Heisenberg-Weyl set, each controlled by a dedicated ancilla qudit. Propositions 1 and 2 prove that arbitrary errors $E = X^a Z^b$ deterministically collapse the ancilla to states $|a \bmod d\rangle$ and $|b \bmod d\rangle$ respectively, enabling syndrome-based detection.
result: For the Mod-2 circuit, PCS provides fidelity improvements of $\approx 20\%$ at $d = 3$ to $\approx 32\%$ at $d = 7$ under $p = 0.3$ depolarizing error; for the two-qudit GHZ-2 circuit, fidelities remain above $97.5\%$ across dimensions at $p = 0.025$, though post-selection overhead grows exponentially with dimension for multi-gate circuits.
